MA 5 350 homes Majority are [11] R-40. 4 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2 Applicability The attic floor insulation upgrade logic is based on a threshold approach, where homes are eligible for retrofit if their existing attic insulation R-value is below the IECC 2021- recommended level for their respective climate zone (Table 2). However, a minimum threshold is set such that the existing R-value must be at least R-10 values lower than the maximum recommended level to qualify for the upgrade. This constraint is applied to avoid inefficient retrofits with marginal benefit, since adding insulation to already well-insulated attics provides diminishing returns in energy savings and may not be cost-effective. Target R-values are assigned by climate zone using DOE-recommended R-values in Table 2 as guidance. Table 3 shows R-values that are typically achieved through retrofits from previous empirical studies. The following logics are applied to existing units: 1. Units have existing attics (automatically exclude multifamily units and mobile homes). 2. Existing attics have an R-value at least R-10 lower than targeted attic insulation level specified for their climate zone in Table 2. 3. Use the upper bound of recommended attic insulation by climate zone in Table 2 to simulate the highest energy savings scenario. Note that in Table 2 and Table 3, the highest bound of R-value range is used in the simulations to represent the most energy-efficient scenarios. Previous studies are referenced to demonstrate that these R-values are reasonable as an upper bound. But, in some cases, our simulations test higher R-values than are typically installed. To determine eligibility for an upgrade, the existing attic must be at least 10 ft²·°F·hr/Btu (R-value) below the target for its climate zone. For example, a unit with existing R-29 won’t get upgraded to R-30 because the marginal benefit of adding 1 R- value is negligible. The R-10 below target rule ensures that upgrades are applied only where they provide meaningful savings. Also, by including only dwellings with attics, this will automatically only include single-family units because ResStock only models attics for single- family units, whereas multifamily models do not include attics.
